title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: In step 5 of a request, your assistant's model uses a booking detail it got from a tool in step 2. Which statement correctly explains how the model has that detail at step 5?

options.text: The model stored the detail internally when it first read the result
The program included the step 2 result in the input of step 5
The model fetched the detail again from the booking system itself
The detail stayed in the model's weights after the step 2 call

items.stem: An assistant request starts with 2,000 tokens (system prompt, tool descriptions and the question). Each of 4 tool steps adds 1,500 tokens to the history. After the 4 tool steps, the model writes its final answer, so there are 5 model calls. Ignoring caching and the tokens the model writes, how many input tokens are processed across all 5 calls?

A student returns to the makerspace a week after their last chat. The assistant program starts a brand-new conversation and saves nothing at the end of sessions. What does the model know about the student's last visit?

options.text: Nothing, because the old context is gone and nothing was saved
Everything, because a large window keeps all past conversations
A summary, because models condense old chats while idle
Only the facts, because the model recognizes returning users

items.stem: A long conversation is close to the context limit. What is the name of the technique of replacing the older history with a model-written summary and continuing from that summary?
The assistant must answer questions from 12 machine manuals totalling about 1,500 pages. Which design best keeps cost per request low while answering from the real manuals?

options.text: Put all 12 manuals in the system prompt, so they are always there
Store the manuals and return only the best-matching passages on request
Ask the model to recite each manual from what it learned in training
Save every manual page into the student's notes at the first visit
